correctness.rationale: The proof exhausts the unit sphere into Euclidean-arc interiors, taxicab-segment interiors, and coordinate-axis junctions. The support-functional characterization of Birkhoff--James orthogonality determines every admissible companion direction in each case. The first two cases are bounded by \(\sqrt2\); the axis case reduces to the maximum of the minimum of one strictly increasing and one strictly decreasing explicit function, so its unique crossing is globally optimal. The crossing is exactly equivalent to \(\tau^4+2\tau^3-1=0\), and the resulting value exceeds \(\sqrt2\). The checker confirms the arithmetic but no finite sample is used as proof.

value.rationale: The source itself flags this exact example as nontrivial and records only a decimal. Converting that benchmark into a closed algebraic value, an explicit exact extremizer, and a complete global proof resolves a concrete gap in a canonical family of Banach-space geometric constants. The result is not an arbitrary numerical slice: the norm is a natural gluing of Euclidean and taxicab geometry used by the defining paper to demonstrate instability of orthogonality-constrained parameters, and the proof exposes why the nonsmooth axis, not the smooth arcs or taxicab edges, controls the invariant.
